correctness.rationale: For positive gap k, the two floor equations give two unit half-open intervals whose displacement has magnitude k*epsilon. Their intersection is empty at and beyond k*epsilon=1. Choosing the smaller endpoint x=−floor(k/2) places the nonempty phase window wholly within [0,q); other x translate it by integer multiples of q and do not intersect that interval. The even windows [j*epsilon,1−j*epsilon) and the sign-dependent odd windows are nested on disjoint phase ranges. Thus N>=m is exactly the union of the even window at gap 2m and the odd one at 2m−1, including the endpoint convention. Counting integers with the resulting weak lower-window and strict upper-window tests gives a floor or ceiling count within one of the triangular height divided by epsilon, with the odd cutoff shifted by at most one mesh cell; [2,q) on the expanding side contributes zero. Setting m=floor(t/epsilon)+1 in the survival formula proves the stated CDF bound by Lipschitz continuity of positive part, and the bounded support gives moment convergence. On N>0 the available gaps are the first N even or odd gaps; coupling the rank to ceil(NV) makes the error relative to 2*epsilon*N*V at most 2*epsilon. The zero-cycle probability tends to zero, so conditioning does not affect the phase limit. Rescaling the phase to [0,2) gives the uniform triangular height independently of V, proving the joint law and the product-of-uniforms marginal. Independent direct iteration also agreed throughout 748 rational phase cells, with 2,534 profile/survival checks in addition to direct gap-list and half-open-cell checks.
residual_risks: Rational-cell checks are finite; the interval and coupling arguments establish the continuum and joint limit. The law is for parameter sampling, not randomly evolving initial states or cycle-weighted parameter sampling.
